skill.name: Agent Browser
skill.description: Automate browser navigation, form entry, page snapshots, and UI checks with the Agent Browser command-line tool.
skill.summary: Automate structured browser tasks from an AI coding assistant.
skill.author: am-will

security_audit.summary: Most external-command alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, and the documented URLs are expected installation or browser-navigation examples. However, the skill explicitly directs users to automate a real Chrome profile and reuse authenticated OAuth sessions. This exposes cookies and active sessions to automated actions and is a critical publication concern.

remediation.issue: The guide instructs users to automate a real Chrome profile with active authenticated sessions.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the real-profile instructions and use a dedicated, unprivileged browser profile or isolated session created solely for automation.

remediation.issue: The guide claims that existing Google and Discord sessions can be reused without login.
remediation.suggestion: Require manual authentication in a visible browser window and warn users never to expose personal, work, or privileged browser profiles.

remediation.issue: The documentation embeds a specific local Chrome profile path.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the personal path with a generic dedicated-profile example and explain how to create it safely.

content.user_title: Automate Browser Tasks with Agent Browser
content.value_statement: Browser workflows can be repetitive and difficult to test manually. Agent Browser provides structured commands for navigation, interaction, snapshots, and UI verification.
actual_capabilities: Open pages and navigate backward, forward, or reload.
Click, fill, select, check, upload, and drag page elements.
Capture page snapshots, screenshots, PDFs, and selected text.
Find elements by role, text, label, placeholder, alt text, title, or test ID.
Wait for selectors, text, URLs, or network idle states.
Run separate browser sessions and return machine-readable snapshots.
limitations: It requires the Agent Browser CLI and its browser dependencies.
Dynamic pages can require explicit waits and refreshed snapshots.
Element references change after navigation and must be captured again.
Do not connect it to personal or privileged browser profiles.

use_cases.title: Test a web form
use_cases.description: Navigate to a staging form, fill fields, submit it, and verify the confirmation state.

use_cases.title: Collect page content
use_cases.description: Open a page, capture a structured snapshot, and extract visible text or attributes.

use_cases.title: Debug an interface
use_cases.description: Use snapshots, screenshots, and element checks to investigate a UI issue.

prompt_templates.title: Open and inspect a page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Agent Browser to open https://example.com and give me an interactive snapshot.

prompt_templates.title: Fill a test form
prompt_templates.prompt: Open the staging contact form, fill the provided test data, submit it, and report the visible result.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a user journey
prompt_templates.prompt: Test the checkout journey on the staging site with test credentials. Take snapshots after each major step and stop before payment confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a UI failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the staging dashboard. Find why the Export button is disabled, capture relevant text and attributes, and suggest a reproducible test.

output_examples.input: Open a page and inspect its controls.
output: Interactive snapshot lists the navigation, search field, and primary action button.

output_examples.input: Fill and submit a test contact form.
output: Form fields were completed with test data.
Submission confirmation is visible on the page.

output_examples.input: Check whether a button is enabled.
output_examples.output: The selected button is visible and enabled.

best_practices: Use a dedicated test account and isolated browser session for automation.
Capture a new snapshot after every navigation before using element references.
Use visible, manual authentication for sensitive services and verify actions before submission.
anti_patterns: Do not connect automation to a personal, work, or privileged Chrome profile.
Do not use stale element references after navigation or major page updates.
Do not automate real purchases, account changes, or irreversible actions without confirmation.

faq.question: What does Agent Browser do?
faq.answer: It provides command-line browser automation for navigation, interaction, page snapshots, and UI checks.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: How do I find page elements?
faq.answer: Create a snapshot, then use its element references or supported text and accessibility selectors.

faq.question: Why should I create a new snapshot after navigation?
faq.answer: Element references are stable only for the current page load and can change after navigation.

faq.question: Can I use my existing Chrome profile?
faq.answer: Do not use a personal or privileged profile. Use an isolated profile and a dedicated test account instead.

faq.question: Can it test authenticated workflows?
faq.answer: Yes, use a dedicated test account and authenticate manually in a visible isolated browser session.
